  - title: Navy Supercarrier USS Gerald R. Ford Is Being Pushed Past the Breaking Point
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/navy-supercarrier-uss-gerald-r-ford-is-being-pushed-passed-the-breaking-point/
    text: With no aircraft carrier currently in CENTCOM, the Navy is weighing options
      as tensions rise with Iran—but the Chief of Naval Operations, Adm. Daryl Caudle,
      is pushing back on extending the USS Gerald R. Ford’s already long deployment.
      Ford has been underway since June 24, 2025, and extending beyond the typical timeline
      risks delayed shipyard maintenance, higher costs, and a readiness hit across the
      entire strike group. The post Navy Supercarrier USS Gerald R. Ford Is Being Pushed
      Past the Breaking Point appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: As tensions with Iran escalate and the Navy lacks an aircraft
      carrier in CENTCOM, Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle is resisting extending
      the USS Gerald R. Ford's lengthy deployment, which could jeopardize maintenance
      and readiness for the entire strike group.
    paragraph_summary: As tensions with Iran escalate, the Navy is considering its options
      in CENTCOM due to the absence of an aircraft carrier, but Chief of Naval Operations
      Adm. Daryl Caudle is resisting the idea of extending the USS Gerald R. Ford's
      deployment, which has been active since June 24, 2025. Extending this deployment
      could lead to delayed maintenance, increased costs, and negatively impact the
      readiness of the entire strike group.
    published: '2026-01-17T12:52:47+00:00'

  - title: 'Did You Know of the Day: The Navy Almost Built Medium Aircraft Carriers
      (CVV)'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/did-you-know-of-the-day-the-navy-almost-built-medium-aircraft-carriers-cvv/
    text: 'The CVV “Aircraft Carrier (Medium)” emerged in the 1970s as the Navy tried
      to balance forward presence with tightening budgets and rising supercarrier costs.
      Envisioned as a conventionally powered carrier in the roughly 52,000–62,000-ton
      range with an air wing of up to about 65 aircraft, CVV aimed to deliver more platforms
      for less money than a Nimitz-class ship. The post Did You Know of the Day: The
      Navy Almost Built Medium Aircraft Carriers (CVV) appeared first on 19FortyFive
      .'
    one_sentence_summary: The CVV "Aircraft Carrier (Medium)" was proposed in the 1970s
      as a cost-effective alternative to supercarriers, designed to be conventionally
      powered and capable of carrying around 65 aircraft, in response to budget constraints
      and rising costs of larger carriers.
    paragraph_summary: The CVV "Aircraft Carrier (Medium)" concept was developed by
      the Navy in the 1970s as a cost-effective solution to maintain forward presence
      amidst budget constraints and increasing expenses associated with supercarriers.
      Designed to be conventionally powered and weighing between 52,000 and 62,000 tons,
      the CVV was intended to support an air wing of approximately 65 aircraft, offering
      a more affordable alternative to the larger Nimitz-class carriers.
    published: '2026-01-17T12:27:41+00:00'

  - title: The U.S. Navy’s Trump-Class Battleship Might Be a ‘Nuclear Bomber’
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-u-s-navys-trump-class-battleship-might-be-a-nuclear-bomber/
    text: 'A proposed Trump-class battleship is framed as a way to refill a naval firepower
      gap—but the bigger question is whether it should carry nuclear capability. The
      argument turns on tradeoffs: adding a mobile surface-launched nuclear option could
      widen presidential choices and complicate an adversary’s targeting calculus, reinforcing
      deterrence if other legs of the force are disrupted. The post The U.S. Navy’s
      Trump-Class Battleship Might Be a ‘Nuclear Bomber’ appeared first on 19FortyFive
      .'
    one_sentence_summary: The proposed Trump-class battleship aims to address naval
      firepower gaps, with a contentious debate over whether it should include nuclear
      capabilities to enhance deterrence and complicate adversary strategies.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the proposal for a Trump-class battleship,
      which aims to address a gap in U.S. naval firepower, while raising the contentious
      issue of whether it should be equipped with nuclear capabilities. Proponents argue
      that incorporating a mobile surface-launched nuclear option could enhance presidential
      decision-making and complicate adversaries' targeting strategies, thereby strengthening
      deterrence, especially if other military assets are compromised. The discussion
      highlights the strategic trade-offs involved in modernizing naval forces.
    published: '2026-01-17T00:20:09+00:00'

  - title: '72,000 Ton Question: The Montana-Class Battleship Is the U.S. Navy’s Big
      ‘What If’'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/72000-ton-question-the-montana-class-battleship-is-the-u-s-navys-big-what-if/
    text: 'The Montana-class battleships sit at the center of a lasting naval “what-if”:
      a larger successor to the Iowa class with heavier armor, a bigger hull, and a
      12-gun 16-inch main battery. They were authorized as the Navy’s final battleship
      order, but the logic of sea power shifted fast. Carrier aviation proved decisive,
      and the Montanas’ slower speed made them ill-suited to operate with fast carrier
      task forces. The post 72,000 Ton Question: The Montana-Class Battleship Is the
      U.S. Navy’s Big ‘What If’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The Montana-class battleships represent a significant naval
      "what-if" scenario as a larger, more heavily armed successor to the Iowa class,
      ultimately rendered obsolete by the rise of carrier aviation and the changing
      dynamics of naval warfare.
    paragraph_summary: The Montana-class battleships represent a significant naval "what-if,"
      envisioned as a larger and more powerful successor to the Iowa class, featuring
      heavier armor, a larger hull, and a formidable 12-gun 16-inch main battery. Although
      they were authorized as the final battleship order for the U.S. Navy, the rapid
      evolution of naval warfare, particularly the rise of carrier aviation, rendered
      them impractical due to their slower speed, which hindered their integration with
      fast carrier task forces. The article explores the implications of this shift
      in naval strategy and the Montana-class battleships' place in naval history.
    published: '2026-01-17T00:03:06+00:00'

  - title: 'U.S. Navy Aircraft Carriers: From Supercarrier to Super Target?'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/u-s-navy-aircraft-carriers-from-supercarrier-to-super-target/
    text: 'Aircraft carriers keep getting declared obsolete as submarines, precision
      missiles, drones, cyber, and space targeting raise the cost of operating at sea.
      But obsolescence is the wrong frame. The strategic environment has shifted from
      permissive wars to peer competition, forcing carriers to change how they fight.
      The post U.S. Navy Aircraft Carriers: From Supercarrier to Super Target? appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article argues that while aircraft carriers are often
      deemed obsolete due to advancements in military technology and changing warfare
      dynamics, they must adapt to new strategic challenges rather than being considered
      outdated.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the evolving role of aircraft carriers
      in modern warfare, highlighting that while they have often been deemed obsolete
      due to advancements in submarines, precision missiles, drones, and cyber warfare,
      this perspective is misguided. Instead of viewing carriers as outdated, the article
      argues that the strategic landscape has transitioned from permissive conflicts
      to peer competition, necessitating a transformation in how carriers operate and
      engage in combat. This shift requires carriers to adapt their strategies to remain
      relevant in a more complex and contested maritime environment.
    published: '2026-01-16T23:47:29+00:00'

  - title: The Boeing X-32 Stealth Fighter ‘What If’ Won’t Go Away
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-boeing-x-32-stealth-fighter-what-if-wont-go-away/
    text: 'Boeing’s X-32 aimed to win JSF on affordability and manufacturing simplicity,
      anchored by a large one-piece delta wing that boosted internal fuel and reduced
      parts count. Test pilots praised its stable, “F/A-18-like” handling, and the program
      moved fast—two variants, dozens of flights, and a clear focus on practical strike
      performance rather than dogfighting flair. The concept also pointed toward advanced
      sensor integration, with radar work that influenced later Navy systems. The decisive
      issue came in the STOVL phase: Lockheed’s lift-fan approach delivered stronger
      vertical-landing performance, while the X-32’s solution struggled with hot exhaust
      recirculation and overheating. The post The Boeing X-32 Stealth Fighter ‘What
      If’ Won’t Go Away appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Boeing's X-32 fighter aimed to secure the Joint Strike Fighter
      contract through affordability and simplicity, featuring a large delta wing and
      stable handling, but ultimately lost to Lockheed's design due to superior vertical-landing
      performance in the STOVL phase.
    paragraph_summary: Boeing's X-32 was designed to secure the Joint Strike Fighter
      (JSF) contract through its affordability and manufacturing simplicity, featuring
      a large one-piece delta wing that enhanced internal fuel capacity and reduced
      parts count. Test pilots noted its stable handling reminiscent of the F/A-18,
      and the program progressed rapidly with two variants and a focus on practical
      strike capabilities over dogfighting. Additionally, the X-32's advanced sensor
      integration and radar developments influenced future Navy systems. However, the
      critical drawback emerged during the Short Takeoff and Vertical Landing (STOVL)
      phase, where Lockheed's lift-fan design outperformed the X-32, which faced challenges
      with hot exhaust recirculation and overheating.
    published: '2026-01-16T23:36:10+00:00'
  - title: The Boeing X-32 Stealth Fighter ‘What If’ Won’t Go Away
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-boeing-x-32-stealth-fighter-what-if-wont-go-away/
    text: 'Boeing’s X-32 aimed to win JSF on affordability and manufacturing simplicity,
      anchored by a large one-piece delta wing that boosted internal fuel and reduced
      parts count. Test pilots praised its stable, “F/A-18-like” handling, and the program
      moved fast—two variants, dozens of flights, and a clear focus on practical strike
      performance rather than dogfighting flair. The concept also pointed toward advanced
      sensor integration, with radar work that influenced later Navy systems. The decisive
      issue came in the STOVL phase: Lockheed’s lift-fan approach delivered stronger
      vertical-landing performance, while the X-32’s solution struggled with hot exhaust
      recirculation and overheating. The post The Boeing X-32 Stealth Fighter ‘What
      If’ Won’t Go Away appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Boeing's X-32 fighter aimed to secure the Joint Strike Fighter
      contract through affordability and simplicity, featuring a large delta wing and
      stable handling, but ultimately lost to Lockheed's design due to superior vertical-landing
      performance in the STOVL phase.
    paragraph_summary: Boeing's X-32 was designed to secure the Joint Strike Fighter
      (JSF) contract through its affordability and manufacturing simplicity, featuring
      a large one-piece delta wing that enhanced internal fuel capacity and reduced
      parts count. Test pilots noted its stable handling reminiscent of the F/A-18,
      and the program progressed rapidly with two variants and a focus on practical
      strike capabilities over dogfighting. Additionally, the X-32's advanced sensor
      integration and radar developments influenced future Navy systems. However, the
      critical drawback emerged during the Short Takeoff and Vertical Landing (STOVL)
      phase, where Lockheed's lift-fan design outperformed the X-32, which faced challenges
      with hot exhaust recirculation and overheating.
    published: '2026-01-16T23:36:10+00:00'

      new approaches in stealth technology, marking a significant, albeit underappreciated,
      contribution to aerospace development.

      drones, missiles, and submarines to deter U.S. carrier strike groups from operating
      within the first island chain.
    paragraph_summary: 'China''s anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) strategy is centered
      around three key components: drones, missiles, and submarines, designed to deter
      U.S. carrier strike groups from operating within the first island chain. This
      strategy includes advanced weaponry such as carrier-killer ballistic missiles
      like the DF-21D and DF-26, sea-skimming YJ-series missiles launched from Type
      055 destroyers and H-6K bombers, as well as stealthier Type 093B and 096 submarines.
      Collectively, these elements create a formidable defense aimed at making the region
      a no-go zone for U.S. naval forces.'

  - title: 'Did You Know: A 45,000-Ton U.S. Navy Iowa-Class Super Battleship Was Never
      Finished and Scrapped'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/did-you-know-a-45000-ton-u-s-navy-iowa-class-super-battleship-was-never-finished-and-scrapped/
    text: 'Summary and Key Points: USS Illinois (BB-65) was envisioned as a new American
      battlewagon built for big-gun dominance—thick armor, heavy displacement, and nine
      16-inch guns meant to punish enemy fleets and support amphibious assaults. But
      the war changed faster than shipyards could. -Pearl Harbor and the carrier battles
      of 1942 pushed naval strategy toward long-range […] The post Did You Know: A 45,000-Ton
      U.S. Navy Iowa-Class Super Battleship Was Never Finished and Scrapped appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The USS Illinois (BB-65), a planned American battleship designed
      for heavy firepower and armor, was ultimately scrapped before completion due to
      shifting naval strategies during World War II.
    paragraph_summary: The USS Illinois (BB-65) was designed as a formidable American
      battleship, featuring heavy armor and nine 16-inch guns aimed at achieving naval
      superiority and supporting ground operations. However, the rapid evolution of
      naval warfare, particularly following the events at Pearl Harbor and the carrier
      battles of 1942, rendered the battleship concept less relevant. As a result, the
      USS Illinois was never completed and was ultimately scrapped, highlighting the
      shifting priorities in naval strategy during World War II.

  - title: The XF-85 Goblin “Parasite Fighter” Has a Message for the U.S. Air Force
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-xf-85-goblin-parasite-fighter-has-a-message-for-the-u-s-air-force/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The XF-85 Goblin was a “parasite fighter” built to
      ride inside a bomber’s bay and launch on demand to protect long-range B-29 and
      B-36 missions when escort fighters lacked the range. -Released on a trapeze, the
      tiny jet was meant to fight off attackers, then reattach to the bomber and […]
      The post The XF-85 Goblin “Parasite Fighter” Has a Message for the U.S. Air Force
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The XF-85 Goblin, a "parasite fighter" designed to be launched
      from and reattached to bombers like the B-29 and B-36 for protection during long
      missions, highlights important lessons for the U.S. Air Force regarding air combat
      strategy.
    paragraph_summary: The XF-85 Goblin was an innovative "parasite fighter" designed
      to be housed within the bomb bay of long-range bombers like the B-29 and B-36,
      providing an on-demand defense mechanism when traditional escort fighters couldn't
      reach the mission area. Released from a trapeze, this compact jet was intended
      to engage enemy aircraft and then return to the bomber for reattachment. The article
      suggests that the lessons learned from the XF-85 Goblin's design and operational
      concept could offer valuable insights for the U.S. Air Force in modern aerial
      combat strategies.
    published: '2026-01-16T16:16:13+00:00'

      and high speed but also significantly boost their operational efficiency and effectiveness
      in combat scenarios.

    text: 'Summary and Key Points – Railguns promised hypersonic projectiles, deep magazines,
      and low cost per shot, but the concept collapsed under shipboard reality: massive
      power bursts, heat, cooling limits, accuracy challenges, and punishing barrel
      erosion. -The deeper issue was integration—Burke-class ships were never built
      for railgun energy demands, and even Zumwalt’s power margin proved finite […]

    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. Navy's railgun concept has failed due to practical
      challenges such as power demands, heat management, and accuracy issues, highlighting
      the need for realistic alternatives like hypersonic missiles.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by the U.S. Navy in
      implementing railgun technology, which was initially promising due to its potential
      for hypersonic projectiles, extensive ammunition capacity, and low cost per shot.
      However, the concept has failed to materialize effectively due to practical issues
      such as the immense power requirements, heat generation, cooling limitations,
      accuracy problems, and significant barrel wear. Furthermore, the integration of
      railguns into existing Burke-class ships was problematic, as they were not designed
      to handle the energy demands, and even the Zumwalt-class ships had limited power
      capacity. Ultimately, the article concludes that while railguns remain unfeasible,
      the development of hypersonic missiles capable of reaching Mach 6 is a tangible
      reality.

      a lack of data transparency.

    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The Army moved to shut down five ceremonial horse

    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. Army initially planned to shut down five ceremonial

    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Army initially decided to shut down five ceremonial
      horse units and put over 200 horses up for adoption to reallocate resources towards
      military readiness and cost savings. However, just days before the new year, this
      decision was partially reversed, allowing the horse programs at Fort Hood and
      Fort Riley to continue, while three other units are still set to be disbanded.
      This situation highlights the ongoing debate about the future of ceremonial horse
      units within the Army.

    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. military has adopted a new Waist-to-Height Ratio

      body fat, replacing the previous height-and-weight tables with a Waist-to-Height
      Ratio (WHtR) approach. According to Under Secretary of War Anthony Tata, service
      members must have a waist measurement that is less than 0.55 times their height
      to meet the new standards. This change aims to provide a more accurate assessment
      of body composition among troops.

    text: 'Summary and Key Points: Researchers from the U.S. Navy, Electric Boat, and

      beams can deeply penetrate thick steel without damaging it, allowing engineers
      to detect internal stress, “ductility dip cracking,” and weld defects […] The

    one_sentence_summary: Researchers have developed a new method using neutron beams
      to inspect submarine hulls for microscopic flaws, enabling the detection of internal
      stress and weld defects without damaging the thick steel.
    paragraph_summary: Researchers from the U.S. Navy, Electric Boat, and the University
      of Connecticut have introduced an innovative technique utilizing neutron beams
      to inspect submarine hulls for microscopic flaws. This method offers significant
      advantages over traditional X-ray inspections, as neutron beams can penetrate
      thick steel without causing damage, enabling the detection of internal stresses,
      ductility dip cracking, and weld defects. This breakthrough enhances the safety
      and reliability of Navy nuclear submarines by providing better protection against
      potential structural issues.

    one_sentence_summary: Professor Alexander Motyl contends that contemporary efforts

      of influence are likely to fail due to the existence of modern states with strong
      militaries and populations committed to national self-determination.
    paragraph_summary: Professor Alexander Motyl contends that contemporary efforts
      by major powers such as the U.S., China, and Russia to recreate 19th-century spheres
      of influence are likely to fail. He argues that unlike the colonial era, today's
      global landscape is characterized by established states with modern military capabilities
      and populations committed to national self-determination. This shift in dynamics
      makes the imposition of spheres of influence increasingly untenable.

  - title: The U.S. Army Encourages Soldiers Now To ‘Just Pick Up’
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-u-s-army-encourages-soldiers-now-to-just-pick-up/
    text: 'Summary and Key Points: In a massive effort to combat suicide over the 2025
      holiday season, U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll launched the “Just Pick Up” campaign,
      directing officers and NCOs to personally check in with every soldier, every day,
      through January 15, 2026. -Inspired by a successful strategy used by the 11th
      Airborne Division […] The post The U.S. Army Encourages Soldiers Now To ‘Just
      Pick Up’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. Army has initiated the "Just Pick Up" campaign, led
      by Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, to encourage daily personal check-ins with every
      soldier to address suicide prevention during the 2025 holiday season.
    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Army has initiated the "Just Pick Up" campaign, spearheaded
      by Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, to address the critical issue of suicide among
      soldiers during the 2025 holiday season. This initiative mandates that officers
      and non-commissioned officers (NCOs) personally check in with every soldier daily
      until January 15, 2026. The campaign draws inspiration from a successful strategy

      for the Navy's future aviation endeavors.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/military-quote-of-the-day-by-socrates-all-wars-are-fought-for-money/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Best known as the father of Western philosophy,
      Socrates was also a disciplined soldier who served as a hoplite in the Peloponnesian
      War, fighting in the battles of Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis. -Despite his
      bravery on the battlefield—where he once saved the life of Alcibiades—Socrates
      famously argued in Plato’s Phaedo […] The post Military Quote of the Day by Socrates:
      ‘All Wars are Fought for Money…’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Socrates, renowned as the father of Western philosophy and
      a courageous hoplite in the Peloponnesian War, controversially stated in Plato's
      Phaedo that all wars are fought for money, despite his own acts of bravery on
      the battlefield.
    paragraph_summary: Socrates, renowned as the father of Western philosophy, was also
      a dedicated soldier who fought as a hoplite in the Peloponnesian War, participating
      in key battles such as Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis, where he notably saved
      Alcibiades' life. Despite his military valor, Socrates expressed a critical view
      of war, famously stating in Plato's "Phaedo" that "All wars are fought for money,"
      highlighting his belief in the underlying economic motivations behind conflict.

      with advanced features such as tailless aerodynamics and adaptive cycle engines,

      aircraft. However, the stagnation in its development raises concerns about the
      Navy's future air combat capabilities.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/the-u-s-air-forces-f-16xl-fighter-mistake-still-stings/
    text: Key Points and Summary on F-16XL Fighter – The F-16XL was a radical “what-if”
      aircraft featuring a cranked-arrow delta wing designed to transform the standard
      F-16 into a high-speed deep strike bomber. -Although it offered superior aerodynamics,
      range, and payload capacity compared to the F-16, the XL ultimately lost the USAF’s
      Enhanced Tactical Fighter competition […] The post The U.S. Air Force’s F-16XL
      Fighter Mistake Still Stings appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The F-16XL, an advanced variant of the F-16 with a cranked-arrow
      delta wing designed for high-speed deep strike missions, ultimately lost the USAF's
      Enhanced Tactical Fighter competition despite its superior aerodynamics, range,
      and payload capacity.
    paragraph_summary: The F-16XL was an innovative variant of the F-16 fighter jet,
      featuring a unique cranked-arrow delta wing design aimed at enhancing its capabilities
      as a high-speed deep strike bomber. While the F-16XL demonstrated superior aerodynamics,
      increased range, and greater payload capacity compared to the standard F-16, it
      ultimately lost out in the U.S. Air Force's Enhanced Tactical Fighter competition.
      This decision is still viewed as a significant oversight, as the aircraft's potential
      benefits remain a topic of discussion among aviation enthusiasts and experts.

      1732 and 1758. The piece emphasizes the importance of taking initiative rather

      and hard work.

    one_sentence_summary: In the 1970s and 80s, the U.S. Navy explored converting Iowa-class

    paragraph_summary: In the 1970s and 80s, the U.S. Navy explored the idea of transforming
      Iowa-class battleships into "battlecarriers" designed to support short takeoff
      and vertical landing (STOVL) aircraft and equipped with significant firepower,
      including 320-tube vertical launch systems. This innovative concept, proposed
      by military reformer Charles E. Myers, aimed to enhance littoral fire support
      capabilities. However, the ambitious "Phase II" plan was ultimately abandoned,
      marking a notable moment in naval history as the Navy reconsidered its approach
      to battleship design and functionality.

      competition to the F-15E Strike Eagle, which was preferred for its twin-engine
      redundancy. Following its defeat, the F-16XL was ultimately retired from military
      consideration and transferred to NASA for further research and development.

      to manually land their aircraft to ensure safety and control during these challenging
      operations.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/social-security-2026-update-new-rules-for-working-while-collecting-benefits/
    text: 'Synopsis: In 2026, retirees can continue to work while collecting Social

    one_sentence_summary: In 2026, retirees can work while receiving Social Security
      benefits, but those under Full Retirement Age face an earnings limit of $24,480,
      with benefits reduced by $1 for every $2 earned over that threshold.
    paragraph_summary: In 2026, retirees will have the option to work while receiving
      Social Security benefits, but there are strict earnings limits for individuals
      under their Full Retirement Age (FRA). The annual earnings cap for that year is
      set at $24,480, with benefits being reduced by $1 for every $2 earned over this
      threshold. For those who reach FRA in 2026, additional rules will apply, impacting
      how their benefits are calculated based on their earnings.

    paragraph_summary: U.S. Army Master Sergeant Jeremy Chambers has made history by
      being promoted directly to the rank of Captain (O-3), bypassing the usual lieutenant
      ranks, in a rare personnel decision supported by Lt. Gen. Jonathan Braga. This
      promotion aims to utilize Chambers' extensive enlisted experience in his new role
      as a Foreign Area Officer (FAO), which necessitates proficiency in foreign languages
      and cultural understanding. Chambers is the first non-commissioned officer (NCO)
      in the U.S. Army to achieve this direct commission as a FAO captain.

      defense expert Christian D. Orr, emphasizing that winning individual battles is
      irrelevant if one ultimately fails to sustain operations.

      between Steve Jobs' business philosophy and military strategy, emphasizing that
      true success lies in survival rather than isolated victories. Jobs famously stated
      that winning individual battles is insignificant if a company runs out of resources
      before delivering a product, a principle he applied throughout his career with
      Apple, Pixar, and his efforts to revitalize Apple. The article highlights the
      importance of maintaining a long-term vision and sustainability in both business
      and military endeavors.

    paragraph_summary: Russia's Su-75 Checkmate, initially promoted with unique marketing

      could serve as a cautionary tale for the U.S. Air Force.

      hands. The U.S. government was concerned that Iran could utilize these "nuclear-capable"
      jets to deliver weapons of mass destruction. The operation highlighted the strategic
      importance of securing military assets in post-Soviet states to mitigate risks
      associated with proliferation.

      access to the reactor, making it far more involved than a simple fuel refill.
    paragraph_summary: Nuclear-powered submarines provide remarkable endurance, but
      their refueling process is complex and time-consuming, requiring the submarine
      to be placed in dry dock and powered down under strict radiation controls. Specialists

      where crews remove and log components for replacement. This intricate industrial
      event can take up to 40 months, highlighting the challenges associated with maintaining
      these advanced vessels.

      integrate advanced technologies from the Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD)

      updates with Block 4 improvements. This proposal emphasizes upgrades in power,
      sensors, computing capabilities, electronic warfare, and manned-unmanned teaming,

      to improve range and thermal performance. However, the article ultimately argues
      that the F-35 will not evolve into the envisioned F-47 NGAD fighter.

      thermal protection, and internal space, indicating that the SR-72 may not fulfill
      the expectations of a traditional bomber role for the U.S. Air Force.

  - title: 'Autopilot Works Until It Doesn’t: The Aircraft Carrier Landing Lesson From
      a U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler Pilot'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/autopilot-works-until-it-doesnt-the-aircraft-carrier-landing-lesson-from-a-u-s-navy-ea-18g-growler-pilot/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Autopilot can be impressive in cruise flight. Still,
      aircraft carrier landings are a different problem: a pitching deck, variable winds,
      and razor-thin margins that punish even minor errors. -Using a former EA-18G Growler
      pilot’s account, this article explains why Naval Aviators distrust full auto-recoveries—and
      why auto-throttle can be flawless for […] The post Autopilot Works Until It Doesn’t:
      The Aircraft Carrier Landing Lesson From a U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler Pilot appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article highlights the limitations of autopilot systems
      in the challenging environment of aircraft carrier landings, emphasizing a former
      EA-18G Growler pilot's perspective on the distrust of full auto-recoveries due
      to the complexities of a pitching deck and variable conditions.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the limitations of autopilot systems in
      the context of aircraft carrier landings, highlighting the challenges posed by
      a moving deck, changing winds, and the need for precision. Using insights from
      a former EA-18G Growler pilot, it emphasizes the skepticism among Naval Aviators
      regarding full auto-recoveries, despite the reliability of auto-throttle systems
      during cruise flight. The piece illustrates that while autopilot can perform well
      in stable conditions, the complexities of carrier landings require a level of
      human judgment and control that automation cannot fully provide.
    published: '2026-01-05T15:06:23+00:00'

  - title: 'Forget the Trump-Class Battleship: The Navy’s Iowa-Class Was Almost an ‘Aircraft
      Carrier’'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/forget-the-trump-class-battleship-the-navys-iowa-class-was-almost-an-aircraft-carrier/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – In the late 1970s and early 1980s, Navy thinkers
      repeatedly revisited a radical idea: convert Iowa-class battleships into ‘battlecarriers’
      or interdiction/assault ships, adding a flight deck for STOVL aircraft and, in
      later concepts, an enormous missile battery—up to a 320-tube VLS—alongside big
      guns and space for Marines and SEALs. -Advocates […] The post Forget the Trump-Class
      Battleship: The Navy’s Iowa-Class Was Almost an ‘Aircraft Carrier’ appeared first
      on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: In the late 1970s and early 1980s, Navy strategists considered
      transforming Iowa-class battleships into hybrid 'battlecarriers' equipped with
      flight decks for STOVL aircraft, extensive missile systems, and space for Marines
      and SEALs.
    paragraph_summary: In the late 1970s and early 1980s, U.S. Navy strategists explored
      the innovative concept of transforming Iowa-class battleships into 'battlecarriers'
      or interdiction/assault ships. This transformation would involve adding a flight
      deck for Short Takeoff and Vertical Landing (STOVL) aircraft, as well as incorporating
      a substantial missile battery—potentially featuring up to 320 Vertical Launch
      System (VLS) tubes—while retaining the battleships' large guns and providing space
      for Marines and SEALs. Advocates of this idea believed it could enhance naval
      capabilities significantly, challenging the notion of traditional battleship roles.
    published: '2026-01-04T13:07:15+00:00'

    text: 'Synopsis: A widely quoted Thomas Jefferson line—“I abhor war and view it

    one_sentence_summary: The article explores how Thomas Jefferson's famous quote about
      abhorring war reflects his belief in it as a necessary evil rather than a moral
      good, emphasizing his recognition of militia responsibilities.
    paragraph_summary: The article examines a famous quote by Thomas Jefferson, "I abhor
      war and view it as the greatest scourge of mankind," suggesting that while it
      may initially seem to express pure pacifism, the full context reveals Jefferson's
      belief that war is a necessary evil rather than a moral good. It emphasizes that
      Jefferson recognized the importance of military responsibilities and the complexities
      of his views on war, challenging the common perception of his stance as entirely
      anti-war.

  - title: Donald Trump’s Venezuela Strike Summed Up in 2 Words
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/donald-trumps-venezuela-strike-summed-up-in-2-words/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The early takes on Venezuela—imperialism, political
      diversion, oil grab—miss the central logic: hemispheric denial. -In 2 Words: Framed
      as the “Donroe Doctrine,” the argument is that Washington will block hostile great-power
      entrenchment in the Western Hemisphere, and Venezuela had become the most advanced
      test case for Russian, Chinese, and Iranian […] The post Donald Trump’s Venezuela
      Strike Summed Up in 2 Words appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article argues that the U.S. response to Venezuela is
      primarily driven by a desire to prevent hostile foreign influence in the region,
      framed as a modern iteration of the Monroe Doctrine.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the U.S. perspective on Venezuela, framing
      it as a critical case in the context of the "Donroe Doctrine," which suggests
      that Washington aims to prevent the influence of hostile great powers like Russia,
      China, and Iran in the Western Hemisphere. It argues that early interpretations
      of the situation—viewing it through the lenses of imperialism, political diversion,
      or oil interests—miss the fundamental issue of hemispheric denial, emphasizing
      that Venezuela has become a significant battleground for geopolitical influence.
    published: '2026-01-04T00:17:57+00:00'

  - title: ‘Ferrari’ F-35 Stealth Fighter Has A Message for the U.S. Air Force
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/ferrari-f-35-stealth-fighter-has-a-message-for-the-u-s-air-force/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Lockheed Martin is pitching a “fifth-generation-plus”
      F-35—an upgraded “Ferrari” variant built by porting select technologies from its

      in tactics, the geopolitical implications and intentions behind U.S. actions in
      Venezuela are distinct from Russia's actions in Ukraine.

      Abraham Lincoln cautioned that the greatest threat to America would not come from

      and tribalism, warning that such sentiments could undermine constitutional liberty
      unless citizens actively uphold their responsibilities to maintain order and respect
      for the law.

  - title: 'Military Quote of the Day by Plato: ‘Only The Dead Have Seen The End Of
      War’'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/military-quote-of-the-day-by-plato-only-the-dead-have-seen-the-end-of-war/
    text: 'Synopsis: “Only the dead have seen the end of war” is widely shared as a
      Plato quote, but the piece argues its real roots trace to George Santayana’s post–World
      War I writing, rejecting the comforting idea that any conflict will truly end
      all others. -The misattribution spread further when Gen. Douglas MacArthur quoted
      the line […] The post Military Quote of the Day by Plato: ‘Only The Dead Have
      Seen The End Of War’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article clarifies that the quote "Only the dead have seen
      the end of war," often misattributed to Plato, actually originates from George
      Santayana's post-World War I writings, emphasizing the idea that conflicts are
      unlikely to ever truly cease.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the misattribution of the quote "Only the
      dead have seen the end of war," often credited to Plato, but actually originating
      from George Santayana's writings after World War I. It highlights how this quote
      challenges the notion that any single conflict can definitively end all wars.
      The misattribution gained further traction when General Douglas MacArthur cited
      the line, reinforcing its prevalence in military discourse despite its true origins.
    published: '2026-01-02T16:27:48+00:00'

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/01/russias-su-35-flanker-has-a-new-enemy-not-the-u-s-air-force/
    text: 'Synopsis: Russia built the Su-35 as a modernized Su-27 and a stopgap while

      despite strong performance and broad interest, because politics and sanctions
      consistently undercut deals. -Now, however, the aircraft’s export story […] The

      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Russia's Su-35, originally developed as an upgraded version
      of the Su-27 and intended for export success, has faced challenges in securing
      international deals due to political factors and sanctions, but its export prospects
      may be changing.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the Su-35 fighter jet, developed by Russia
      as an upgraded version of the Su-27, intended to serve as a temporary solution
      while the country pursued fifth-generation aircraft. Despite its strong performance
      and initial interest from potential buyers, the expected surge in exports did
      not materialize due to political factors and sanctions that hindered international
      deals. However, the article suggests that the Su-35 now faces a new challenge
      in the export market, indicating a shift in the competitive landscape for this
      aircraft.

      that it is not a fifth-generation fighter but rather an advanced iteration of
      the Su-27 Flanker, designed to serve as a stopgap while the more advanced Su-57
      is still in development. The Su-35 boasts impressive capabilities, including long
      range, heavy payload, and exceptional maneuverability, supported by advanced radar
      and infrared search and track systems. However, it falls short in terms of true
      stealth and integrated networking capabilities, which are essential features found
      in fifth-generation fighters like the F-22 and F-35.

      which aims to feature a large missile magazine on a single hull, drawing parallels

      Nakhimov, whose lengthy modernization process exemplifies the pitfalls of mega-surface
      combatants, which can become costly to upgrade, difficult to protect, and slow
      to deploy back into service. Despite advancements in long-range missiles and enhanced
      defenses, the article suggests that such large vessels may ultimately be more
      of a financial burden than a strategic asset for naval forces.

      fighter program aimed at replacing the Rafale and Eurofighter fleets by 2040,
      has encountered significant delays, missing another decision deadline without

      the initiative has stalled due to ongoing conflicts between France's Dassault

      the FCAS may never materialize, potentially benefiting competitors like the F-35
      and F-47.

      featuring the F-47 NGAD as a deep-penetrating leader, supported by loyal-wingman
      drones, alongside upgrades for the F-22 and F-35 to enhance overall combat effectiveness.
    paragraph_summary: The Air Force is transitioning to a three-tier air-dominance
      model, moving away from reliance on a single aircraft. Central to this strategy
      is the F-47 NGAD, designed as a deep-penetrating quarterback for contested environments,
      and intended to integrate with a broader system that includes loyal-wingman drones.
      Additionally, there are plans for a viability upgrade package to enhance existing
      aircraft capabilities, such as the F-22 and F-35, which will serve as enforcers
      and quarterbacks, respectively, in this new operational framework.

    one_sentence_summary: China is enhancing its airpower capabilities by developing
      advanced aerial refueling tankers like the Y-20U, which significantly extend the
      operational range of its stealth fighters, the J-20 and J-35.

      not only developing advanced stealth fighters like the J-20 and J-35 but also
      by investing in crucial support systems such as a new generation of aerial refueling
      tankers, particularly the Y-20U. This strategic focus on refueling technology
      enables these fighters to extend their operational range and duration, allowing

      capabilities are poised to rival those of the U.S. F-22 and F-35, potentially
      doubling the effective range of its stealth aircraft.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/forget-the-f-22-of-f-35-the-air-forces-new-6th-gen-f-47-ngad-is-coming/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Boeing’s F-47 sits at the center of the U.S. NGAD

  - title: The U.S. Navy Is One Giant Pressure Cooker Sailing Into 2026
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-u-s-navy-is-one-giant-pressure-cooker-sailing-into-2026/
    text: Key points and Summary – Is the U.S. Navy in crisis? Not quite—but the strain
      is increasingly visible. -Procurement misfires like Zumwalt and LCS produced costly
      micro-fleets and early retirements, while constant concept churn signals uncertainty
      about what future naval warfare demands. -Aircraft carriers remain the centerpiece
      for power projection, yet China’s A2/AD environment is […] The post The U.S. Navy
      Is One Giant Pressure Cooker Sailing Into 2026 appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. Navy is facing increasing strain due to procurement
      issues and uncertainty in naval warfare concepts, while aircraft carriers continue
      to be central to power projection amid challenges posed by China's A2/AD environment.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the current state of the U.S. Navy, suggesting
      that while it is not in outright crisis, it is under increasing strain due to
      various challenges. Procurement issues, exemplified by projects like the Zumwalt
      and Littoral Combat Ship (LCS), have led to costly micro-fleets and premature
      retirements of vessels. Additionally, ongoing shifts in naval warfare concepts
      indicate uncertainty about future needs. Although aircraft carriers continue to
      play a crucial role in power projection, the growing anti-access/area denial (A2/AD)
      capabilities of China pose significant challenges. Overall, the Navy is likened
      to a pressure cooker, facing mounting pressures as it approaches 2026.
    published: '2025-12-30T21:16:57+00:00'

      higher per-unit and lifecycle costs are exacerbated by its multinational management,
      although the cost disparity is not as extreme as claimed.
    paragraph_summary: The French National Assembly has reignited the ongoing debate
      over the costs of the Rafale versus the Eurofighter, asserting that the Eurofighter's
      per-unit and lifecycle expenses are significantly higher, largely due to inefficiencies
      linked to its multinational management structure. While the article presents procurement
      figures that highlight a substantial cost disparity, it clarifies that the costs
      are not as extreme as the claim that the Eurofighter is "twice as expensive" as
      the Rafale. The timing of this discussion is critical as it unfolds amidst the
      broader context of the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) fighter program.

    text: 'Synopsis: While China’s J-20 and J-35A stealth fighters collect headlines

    one_sentence_summary: Boeing claims that the U.S. Air Force's F-47 sixth-generation
      fighter has already entered production, despite being publicly unveiled in March
      2025, suggesting that the Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD) program began years
      earlier than indicated.
    paragraph_summary: Boeing has announced that the U.S. Air Force's F-47 sixth-generation
      fighter, part of the Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD) program, has already
      entered production, despite being publicly unveiled in March 2025. This claim
      suggests that the NGAD program's development began years earlier than officially
      acknowledged. While China's J-20 and J-35A stealth fighters have garnered significant
      attention, Boeing's assertion indicates that the U.S. is advancing its own cutting-edge
      fighter technology more rapidly than previously thought.

  - title: 'Quote of the Day by President Herbert Hoover: ‘Older men declare war. But
      it is youth that must fight and die…’:'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/quote-of-the-day-by-president-herbert-hoover-older-men-declare-war-but-it-is-youth-that-must-fight-and-die/
    text: 'Synopsis: Herbert Hoover’s 1944 warning—“Older men declare war… but it is
      youth that must fight and die”—captures a timeless imbalance at the heart of democratic
      warfare: those who authorize conflict rarely bear its physical costs. -In World
      War II, Hoover feared political leaders could become insulated from the brutality
      paid by young servicemembers and their […] The post Quote of the Day by President
      Herbert Hoover: ‘Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die…’:
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Herbert Hoover's 1944 statement highlights the enduring disparity
      in democratic warfare, where older leaders initiate conflicts while the burden
      of fighting and dying falls on the youth.
    paragraph_summary: The article reflects on Herbert Hoover's 1944 statement highlighting
      the disconnect between political leaders who declare wars and the young individuals
      who are compelled to fight and sacrifice their lives. It emphasizes the enduring
      issue within democratic societies where decision-makers often remain shielded
      from the harsh realities of warfare, leaving the burden of conflict to the youth.
      Hoover's concerns during World War II resonate with contemporary discussions about
      the moral responsibilities of those in power when it comes to the consequences
      of their decisions on the lives of young servicemembers.
    published: '2025-12-29T23:30:52+00:00'

  - title: The U.S. Navy’s Trump-Class Battleship Will Be ‘Quietly Shelved’
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-u-s-navys-trump-class-battleship-will-be-quietly-shelved/
    text: 'Synopsis: President Trump’s proposed Trump-class “guided-missile battleship”
      (BBG(X)) is designed to be a headline-grabbing symbol of revived naval power,
      but it collides with how modern maritime combat actually works. -The concept is
      missile-centric—closer to an oversized destroyer than to a traditional armored
      battleship—and it would concentrate expensive capabilities into an obvious, high-priority
      target, making it […] The post The U.S. Navy’s Trump-Class Battleship Will Be
      ‘Quietly Shelved’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: President Trump's proposed Trump-class guided-missile battleship,
      intended to symbolize renewed naval strength, is likely to be abandoned due to
      its misalignment with modern maritime combat strategies and its vulnerability
      as a high-priority target.
    paragraph_summary: President Trump's proposed Trump-class "guided-missile battleship"
      (BBG(X)) aims to serve as a striking emblem of renewed naval strength; however,
      it fundamentally misaligns with contemporary maritime combat realities. The design
      is more missile-focused, resembling a large destroyer rather than a classic armored
      battleship, and it risks concentrating costly capabilities into a single, easily
      identifiable target. As a result, experts suggest that the project is likely to
      be "quietly shelved" due to its impracticality in modern warfare.
    published: '2025-12-29T23:16:11+00:00'

  - title: The U.S. Air Force Might Not Be ‘Ready’ for a War
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-u-s-air-force-might-not-be-ready-for-a-war/
    text: 'Synopsis: A new Pentagon Inspector General audit found F-35 aircraft availability
      averaged about 50% in fiscal year 2024, underscoring persistent sustainment and
      oversight shortcomings in the program’s contractor-driven support model. -The
      issue is broader than one fighter: Air Force-wide mission capable rates fell to
      roughly 67% in FY2024, the lowest in at least a decade, […] The post The U.S.
      Air Force Might Not Be ‘Ready’ for a War appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: A Pentagon Inspector General audit revealed that F-35 aircraft
      availability averaged only 50% in fiscal year 2024, highlighting ongoing sustainment
      issues and contributing to the Air Force's overall mission capable rate dropping
      to its lowest in a decade at approximately 67%.
    paragraph_summary: A recent audit by the Pentagon Inspector General revealed that
      the availability of F-35 aircraft averaged only 50% in fiscal year 2024, highlighting
      ongoing issues with sustainment and oversight within the program's contractor-driven
      support model. This problem extends beyond the F-35, as the overall mission-capable
      rates for the Air Force dropped to approximately 67%, marking the lowest levels
      in at least ten years. These findings raise concerns about the U.S. Air Force's
      preparedness for potential conflicts.
    published: '2025-12-29T20:17:10+00:00'

    one_sentence_summary: The article highlights Volodymyr Zelensky's pivotal decision
      during the February 2022 crisis, where he prioritized the need for military support
      over evacuation, thereby boosting national morale and reframing Western aid as
      assistance for Ukraine's defense.
    paragraph_summary: The article highlights Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's
      pivotal decision during the imminent threat of a Russian attack in February 2022,
      where he famously rejected offers for evacuation assistance in favor of requesting
      military support, stating, "I need ammunition, not a ride." This response not
      only served to boost morale among Ukrainians but also denied Russia a quick propaganda
      victory and reframed Western aid as a means of supporting Ukraine's self-defense
      efforts. Zelensky's stance became a defining moment in the conflict, emphasizing
      resilience and determination in the face of aggression.

    text: 'Synopsis: The USS Abraham Lincoln’s rapid move from San Diego to Guam and

      presence near China even if one is at home port. -Combined with the forward deployment

    one_sentence_summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln's swift deployment to the Philippine
      Sea, alongside the USS George Washington in Japan, enhances the U.S. Navy's presence
      in the Western Pacific with two aircraft carriers near China, complemented by
      the forward deployment of the USS Tripoli and stealth F-35 fighters.
    paragraph_summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln has swiftly transitioned from San Diego
      to Guam and is currently operating in the Philippine Sea, joining the USS George
      Washington, which is stationed in Japan. This deployment establishes a dual U.S.
      supercarrier presence in the Western Pacific, strategically positioned near China,
      despite one carrier being at its home port. Additionally, the forward deployment
      of the USS Tripoli and the presence of stealth F-35 fighters further enhance the
      U.S. military's capabilities in the region, signaling a robust naval posture in
      China's vicinity.

  - title: Ukraine’s War May End Like the Korean War, Not a Treaty
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/ukraines-war-may-end-like-the-korean-war-not-a-treaty/
    text: 'Synopsis: The much-hyped “Mar-a-Lago peace deal” is not a peace deal at all—only
      a political gesture between Washington and Kyiv that leaves the core disputes
      untouched. -The war’s real obstacles remain the same: irreconcilable territorial
      demands, incompatible security guarantees, and the high-stakes question of control
      over the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. -Because neither Moscow nor Kyiv […] The
      post Ukraine’s War May End Like the Korean War, Not a Treaty appeared first on
      19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The so-called "Mar-a-Lago peace deal" is merely a political
      gesture that fails to address the fundamental issues of the Ukraine war, suggesting
      that its resolution may resemble the unresolved nature of the Korean War rather
      than a formal treaty.
    paragraph_summary: The article critiques the so-called "Mar-a-Lago peace deal,"
      describing it as merely a political gesture between Washington and Kyiv rather
      than a genuine peace agreement. It argues that the fundamental issues driving
      the Ukraine conflict—such as conflicting territorial claims, incompatible security
      guarantees, and the contentious control of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant—remain
      unresolved. The piece suggests that, like the Korean War, the conflict in Ukraine
      may ultimately end without a formal treaty, leaving the core disputes intact.
    published: '2025-12-29T18:17:45+00:00'

      a 1969 episode of "Star Trek." This misattribution highlights how pop culture

      of verifying the sources of famous quotes.

      targets before adversaries are aware of its presence. While the F-22 is recognized
      as the best in terms of pure air combat performance, the F-35's superior situational
      awareness and targeting capabilities solidify its position as the most powerful
      fighter jet.

    paragraph_summary: In his 2002 speech in Chicago, then-Illinois state senator Barack
      Obama articulated his opposition to the impending Iraq War by condemning it as
      a "dumb" and "rash" conflict, driven more by emotion and political motives than
      by clear national interests. This stance not only propelled Obama into the national
      spotlight but also foreshadowed his future foreign policy approach, which emphasized
      realism and strategic considerations. His famous quote, "I don’t oppose all wars.
      What I am opposed to is a dumb war," encapsulated his nuanced perspective on military
      engagement.

  - title: Why Germany Is Doubling Down on the F-35 Stealth Fighter
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/why-germany-is-doubling-down-on-the-f-35-stealth-fighter/
    text: 'Synopsis: Germany’s commitment to the F-35 stands apart from some European
      partners weighing non-U.S. alternatives, and it stems from specific strategic
      realities. -The central driver is NATO’s nuclear-sharing mission and the need
      to replace aging Tornado aircraft with a platform that can meet those obligations
      without a prolonged certification gap. -Berlin’s broader Zeitenwende military
      reset […] The post Why Germany Is Doubling Down on the F-35 Stealth Fighter appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Germany's decision to invest in the F-35 stealth fighter,
      unlike some European partners considering non-U.S. options, is driven by its NATO
      nuclear-sharing responsibilities and the urgent need to replace aging Tornado
      aircraft as part of its military modernization efforts.
    paragraph_summary: Germany's decision to invest in the F-35 stealth fighter distinguishes
      it from some European allies considering alternatives, primarily due to strategic
      necessities linked to NATO's nuclear-sharing mission. The need to replace its
      aging Tornado aircraft with a capable platform that fulfills these obligations
      without significant certification delays is a key factor. Additionally, this move
      aligns with Berlin's broader military reset, known as Zeitenwende, emphasizing
      a commitment to modernizing its defense capabilities.
    published: '2025-12-29T15:16:24+00:00'

      strategic capabilities during World War II.

    text: 'Synopsis: The Air Force’s long-running “bomber deficit” is resurfacing as
      global tasking grows faster than available, ready aircraft. -The central risk
      is timing: legacy bombers like the B-1B, B-52, and B-2 are aging, while the B-21’s
      production ramp remains uncertain. -If retirements outpace deliveries, the service
      could face a serious readiness gap. -The counterargument is […] The post The Air
      Force’s Bomber Gap Is Back—and the New B-21 Raider May Not Arrive Fast Enough
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The Air Force is facing a renewed "bomber deficit" as the
      demand for global missions increases faster than the availability of aging aircraft,
      with concerns that the delivery of the new B-21 Raider may not keep pace with
      retirements of older bombers, potentially leading to a significant readiness gap.
    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Air Force is grappling with a renewed "bomber deficit"
      as the demand for global operations outpaces the availability of ready aircraft.
      With legacy bombers such as the B-1B, B-52, and B-2 aging and the production of
      the new B-21 Raider uncertain, there is a risk that retirements could outstrip
      deliveries, leading to a significant readiness gap. While some argue that the
      situation can be managed, the timing of the B-21's arrival is critical to addressing
      this potential shortfall in bomber capabilities.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/how-do-you-sink-a-13000000000-navy-aircraft-carrier-a-15000000-missile-from-china/
    text: 'Synopsis: China’s anti-access strategy in a Taiwan war hinges on denying

      fire. -Three systems anchor the “carrier-killer” concept: the DF-21D for strikes
      inside the First Island Chain, the longer-range DF-26B designed to hold Guam and
      distant forces at risk, and the DF-17 hypersonic […] The post How Do You Sink
      a $13,000,000,000 Navy Aircraft Carrier? A $15,000,000 Missile from China appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: China's anti-access strategy in a potential Taiwan conflict
      relies on a "carrier-killer" approach that employs advanced missile systems, including
      the DF-21D, DF-26B, and DF-17, to prevent U.S. carrier strike groups from entering
      the Western Pacific.
    paragraph_summary: 'China''s anti-access strategy in a potential conflict over Taiwan
      focuses on preventing U.S. carrier strike groups from entering the Western Pacific
      through extensive missile attacks. This strategy is supported by three key missile
      systems: the DF-21D, which targets areas within the First Island Chain; the DF-26B,
      designed to threaten Guam and other distant military assets; and the DF-17 hypersonic
      missile, which enhances China''s capability to strike quickly and effectively.
      The article highlights the stark contrast in cost between a U.S. aircraft carrier,
      valued at approximately $13 billion, and the relatively low cost of a Chinese
      missile, priced at around $15 million, underscoring the potential for significant
      asymmetrical warfare dynamics.'

      World War III will be fought, but World War IV…’'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/military-quote-of-the-day-by-albert-einstein-i-know-not-with-what-weapons-world-war-iii-will-be-fought-but-world-war-iv/
    text: 'Synopsis: Albert Einstein’s famous warning—World War IV fought with “sticks
      and stones”—has become shorthand for the idea that a nuclear war would collapse
      civilization back to primitive violence. -The quote’s popularity surged anew after
      Oppenheimer, but its origin is less clean than many assume. -Einstein spent decades
      wrestling with war: opposing militarism in World War […] The post Military Quote
      of the Day By Albert Einstein: ‘I know not with what weapons World War III will
      be fought, but World War IV…’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Albert Einstein's warning that World War IV would be fought
      with "sticks and stones" underscores the catastrophic consequences of nuclear
      war, a sentiment that has gained renewed attention following the film "Oppenheimer,"
      despite the complexities surrounding the quote's origin and Einstein's long-standing
      opposition to militarism.
    paragraph_summary: Albert Einstein's cautionary statement about World War IV being
      fought with "sticks and stones" serves as a powerful reminder of the potential
      devastation of nuclear war, suggesting that such a conflict could regress civilization
      to primitive states. This quote has gained renewed attention following the release
      of the film "Oppenheimer," yet its origins are more complex than commonly believed.
      Throughout his life, Einstein grappled with the implications of war and consistently
      opposed militarism, particularly during World War I and II, reflecting his deep
      concerns about the future of humanity in the face of escalating violence and technological
      warfare.

      concept to transform Iowa-class battleships into hybrid aircraft carriers, dubbed
      "battlecarriers." This idea aimed to equip the battleships with a flight deck
      capable of launching Short Takeoff and Vertical Landing (STOVL) jets, blending
      the firepower of traditional battleships with the versatility of aircraft carriers.
      While the Navy currently focuses on new battleship designs, the historical notion
      of repurposing Iowa-class vessels highlights the evolving strategies and innovations
      in naval warfare.

      X-35 ultimately favored over Boeing's X-32 due to its superior STOVL capabilities

    paragraph_summary: The Joint Strike Fighter competition, held from 1997 to 2001,
      sought to develop a single family of stealth aircraft suitable for the Air Force,
      Navy, Marine Corps, and allied nations, with an emphasis on reducing maintenance
      costs. In the final phase, Lockheed's X-35 and Boeing's X-32 competed, with the
      X-35's design requiring fewer modifications for short takeoff and vertical landing
      (STOVL) capabilities, which became a key differentiator in the selection process.
      The article suggests that the X-32 stealth fighter has relevant implications for
      the U.S. Air Force, especially in light of advancements like China's J-20 and
      J-35A aircraft.

    text: 'Synopsis: The F-22 Raptor still represents the gold standard for air dominance,

      .'
    one_sentence_summary: The Air Force claims that reviving the F-22 Raptor, despite
      its status as a premier air dominance fighter, is impractical due to the loss
      of its industrial base and the substantial costs required to restart production.
    paragraph_summary: The F-22 Raptor is still considered the benchmark for air superiority;
      however, the U.S. Air Force contends that reviving its production is impractical.
      Recent studies presented to Congress reveal that the Raptor's industrial infrastructure
      has deteriorated, with essential tooling and suppliers no longer available. Restarting
      production would necessitate billions of dollars in investment before any new
      aircraft could be completed, making the prospect of building new F-22 stealth
      fighters unfeasible.

      by deploying aircraft carriers, including the USS George Washington and USS Abraham
      Lincoln, to strengthen alliances and improve crisis response capabilities near
      China.
    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Navy is enhancing its presence in the Indo-Pacific region
      after years focused on the Middle East by deploying a forward-deployed aircraft
      carrier, the USS George Washington, back to Yokosuka following its midlife refueling,

      in the area, signaling a strategic shift aimed at countering China's influence.
      This renewed focus includes the integration of stealth F-35s, emphasizing the
      Navy's commitment to maintaining a robust military posture in close proximity
      to China.

    text: 'Synopsis: China’s airpower story is no longer only about stealth fighters—it’s

    one_sentence_summary: China's airpower strategy is evolving beyond stealth fighters
      to include advanced aerial refueling capabilities, significantly enhancing the
      operational range and effectiveness of its J-20 and new J-35 stealth fighters.
    paragraph_summary: China's airpower capabilities are evolving beyond just stealth
      fighters, focusing on the critical enablers that enhance their operational reach,
      particularly through aerial refueling. This advancement allows for extended loiter
      times, increased route flexibility, and less dependence on external fuel tanks
      that can compromise stealth. The People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) is
      modernizing its fleet, moving from older H-6U tankers to more advanced systems,
      which could significantly enhance the range and effectiveness of their stealth
      fighters, such as the J-20 and the new J-35, potentially doubling their operational
      range and posing a greater challenge to U.S. aircraft like the F-22 and F-35.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/it-could-twist-apart-russia-only-built-1-su-47-berkut-stealth-fighter/
    text: 'Synopsis: Forward-swept wings promise sharp subsonic agility, better lift
      behavior, and shorter takeoffs—exactly why designers flirted with them for carrier
      and air-superiority fighters. But both Russia’s Su-47 and America’s X-29 proved
      the same point: the aerodynamics work, the structure is the problem. -Without
      fly-by-wire, the layout is brutally unstable; with it, the jet can fly, […] The
      post It Could Twist Apart: Russia Only Built 1 Su-47 Berkut ‘Stealth’ Fighter
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Forward-swept wings enhance agility and lift in fighter jets,
      but the structural challenges they pose, as demonstrated by Russia's Su-47 and
      America's X-29, limit their practical application despite successful aerodynamics.
    paragraph_summary: Forward-swept wings offer advantages like enhanced agility, improved
      lift, and shorter takeoff distances, making them appealing for military aircraft
      design, particularly for carrier and air-superiority fighters. However, both Russia's
      Su-47 and America's X-29 have demonstrated that while the aerodynamics of such
      designs are effective, structural challenges pose significant issues. The Su-47,
      known for its stealth capabilities, was ultimately limited to a single prototype
      due to its inherent instability without fly-by-wire technology, which is necessary
      for safe flight but complicates the aircraft's structural integrity.
    published: '2025-12-27T14:57:37+00:00'

  - title: U.S. Air Force Mach 3 SR-71 Blackbird Was Needed Secret ‘Custom Fuel’ to
      Fly
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/u-s-air-force-mach-3-sr-71-blackbird-was-needed-secret-custom-fuel-to-fly/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The SR-71 Blackbird didn’t just demand exotic titanium
      and hand-built parts—it needed a fuel system unlike anything else in U.S. aviation.
      -Conventional jet fuel risked catastrophic fire at Mach 3, so engineers created
      JP-7, a stable kerosene-based blend so resistant to ignition it could shrug off
      an open flame. -To […] The post U.S. Air Force Mach 3 SR-71 Blackbird Was Needed
      Secret ‘Custom Fuel’ to Fly appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The SR-71 Blackbird required a unique fuel, JP-7, specifically
      designed to withstand the extreme conditions of Mach 3 flight and prevent ignition,
      unlike conventional jet fuels.
    paragraph_summary: The SR-71 Blackbird, a Mach 3 reconnaissance aircraft, required
      a unique fuel system due to the risks associated with conventional jet fuel at
      such high speeds. Engineers developed JP-7, a specialized kerosene-based fuel
      blend that was highly resistant to ignition, allowing the aircraft to operate
      safely without the threat of catastrophic fires. This custom fuel was essential
      for the SR-71's performance and safety, highlighting the advanced engineering
      required for this groundbreaking aircraft.

  - title: 'Military Quote of the Day by General Carl von Clausewitz: “Never forget
      that no military leader has ever become great without…”'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/military-quote-of-the-day-by-general-carl-von-clausewitz-never-forget-that-no-military-leader-has-ever-become-great-without/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Carl von Clausewitz rose from a young Prussian cadet
      to a battlefield-tested officer shaped by the Napoleonic age. -Mentored by reformers
      like Scharnhorst, he watched Prussia collapse at Jena and Auerstedt—an experience
      that pushed him to rethink how states fight and why they win. -In 1812 he resigned
      rather than […] The post Military Quote of the Day by General Carl von Clausewitz:
      “Never forget that no military leader has ever become great without…” appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Carl von Clausewitz, influenced by his experiences as a Prussian
      officer during the Napoleonic Wars and mentorship from military reformers, redefined
      military strategy and leadership, ultimately resigning in 1812 to reflect on the
      nature of warfare.
    paragraph_summary: Carl von Clausewitz, who evolved from a young Prussian cadet
      to a seasoned officer during the Napoleonic Wars, was significantly influenced
      by reformers like Scharnhorst and the devastating defeats Prussia faced at Jena
      and Auerstedt. These experiences prompted him to critically reassess the nature
      of warfare and the factors that contribute to a state's success in battle. In
      1812, he made the decision to resign, reflecting his deep convictions about military
      strategy and leadership. The article concludes with a notable quote from Clausewitz
      emphasizing the importance of foundational principles in military leadership.

    text: 'Synopsis: This piece traces the rise and fall of the Soviet Kirov-class battlecruisers,

      embodied Moscow’s blue-water ambitions. -But post–Cold War budget collapse, aging
      […] The post Kirov-Class: Russia’s Nuclear ‘Carrier Killer’ Battlecruiser That
      Never Fired a Shot appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article explores the history of the Soviet Kirov-class
      battlecruisers, highlighting their impressive capabilities as nuclear-powered
      warships designed to challenge NATO, while also detailing their decline due to
      post-Cold War budget issues and aging technology.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the history of the Soviet Kirov-class battlecruisers,
      massive nuclear-powered vessels designed to challenge NATO carrier groups and
      spearhead Soviet naval operations. Equipped with formidable Granit anti-ship missiles,
      heavy artillery, robust armor, and anti-submarine warfare helicopters, the Kirovs
      represented the Soviet Union's aspirations for a powerful blue-water navy. However,
      following the Cold War, financial constraints and the aging of these ships led
      to their decline, ultimately resulting in the Kirovs never having engaged in combat
      despite their intimidating capabilities.

    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The loss of the USS Scorpion (SSN-589) submarine
      remains one of the U.S. Navy’s most haunting unsolved mysteries, claiming 99 lives

      on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The USS Scorpion, a U.S. Navy nuclear submarine, mysteriously
      sank near the Azores in May 1968, resulting in the loss of 99 lives, with its
      wreckage later found imploded at a depth of 10,000 feet.
    paragraph_summary: The USS Scorpion (SSN-589), a U.S. Navy nuclear submarine, tragically
      sank in May 1968, resulting in the loss of 99 crew members, and remains one of
      the Navy's most perplexing mysteries. The submarine disappeared while returning
      from the Mediterranean near the Azores, and its wreckage was later found at a
      depth of 10,000 feet, having imploded. The circumstances surrounding its disappearance
      and the reasons for the implosion continue to evoke intrigue and speculation.

  - title: 'Forget the J-20 and J-35A: China’s Stealth Fighters are No Match for the
      F-22 or F-35'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/forget-the-j-20-and-j-35a-chinas-stealth-fighters-are-no-match-for-the-f-22-or-f-35/
    text: 'Synopsis: This piece examines China’s rapid push to field fifth-generation
      fighters like the J-20 and upcoming J-35A, and asks whether it truly threatens
      U.S. air dominance. -Beijing is proving it can design and mass-produce stealth
      jets, extend their range, and build up supporting tankers. But the article argues
      that numbers alone don’t equal parity. -The […] The post Forget the J-20 and J-35A:
      China’s Stealth Fighters are No Match for the F-22 or F-35 appeared first on 19FortyFive
      .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article analyzes China's advancements in fifth-generation
      fighter jets like the J-20 and J-35A, suggesting that despite their rapid development
      and production capabilities, they do not pose a significant threat to U.S. air
      dominance represented by the F-22 and F-35.
    paragraph_summary: The article analyzes China's swift development of fifth-generation
      fighters, particularly the J-20 and the forthcoming J-35A, questioning their potential
      to challenge U.S. air superiority. While it highlights China's advancements in
      designing and mass-producing stealth aircraft, enhancing their range, and developing
      support tankers, it contends that numerical strength does not equate to operational
      parity. Ultimately, the piece asserts that China's stealth fighters are unlikely
      to match the capabilities of the U.S. F-22 and F-35.
    published: '2025-12-26T19:41:17+00:00'

  - title: The Ukraine War Will Decide Putin’s Fate
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-ukraine-war-will-decide-putins-fate/
    text: 'Synopsis: This piece explores how the outcome of the Ukraine war will shape
      Vladimir Putin’s political future and Russia’s trajectory. -A frozen conflict
      or armistice that locks in limited territorial gains could let the Kremlin sell
      “not losing” as victory, entrenching a poorer, more militarized Russia under a
      tired strongman. -A clearer battlefield setback, by contrast, […] The post The
      Ukraine War Will Decide Putin’s Fate appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article examines how the resolution of the Ukraine war
      will influence Vladimir Putin's political future and Russia's direction, suggesting
      that a stalemate could allow the Kremlin to frame a limited victory, while a significant
      defeat could undermine his leadership.
    paragraph_summary: The article examines the implications of the Ukraine war on Vladimir
      Putin's political future and Russia's direction. It suggests that a frozen conflict
      or armistice, which secures limited territorial gains for Russia, could allow
      the Kremlin to portray a narrative of "not losing" as a victory, potentially leading
      to a more impoverished and militarized Russia under a weary leader. Conversely,
      a significant defeat on the battlefield could have more severe consequences for
      Putin's regime, indicating that the war's outcome is pivotal for both his leadership
      and the country's trajectory.
    published: '2025-12-26T19:16:14+00:00'

      and B-21 Raider.

      the country's first genuine long-range, nuclear-capable strategic bomber, potentially
      threatening U.S. military bases as far away as Guam and Hawaii. While the H-20
